recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中，粉紅色壞死／纖維素樣區域周圍的組織球空泡內可見成群、約 2–4 µm 的圓形小體，中心深染且外圍有透明暈，符合組織漿菌（Histoplasma）。
features: Central area of pale eosinophilic granular necrotic/fibrinoid material
Clusters of small uniform round-to-oval organisms (about 2-4 um) with a dark central dot and surrounding clear halo, within histiocyte vacuoles and at the edge of necrosis
Surrounding histiocytes with oval to reniform, folded nuclei and vesicular chromatin
Scattered small lymphocytes and occasional golden-brown pigment (likely hemosiderin)
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows an area of eosinophilic necrosis bordered by histiocytes with folded, vesicular nuclei and scattered lymphocytes. Within histiocyte cytoplasmic vacuoles and at the edge of the necrotic area are clusters of small, uniform round-to-oval organisms with central basophilic dots and clear halos, measuring approximately 2-4 um. No hyphae are seen. Findings are consistent with histiocytic/necrotizing inflammation with intracellular yeasts suggestive of Histoplasma capsulatum; GMS and PAS stains and culture are recommended for confirmation.

ddx.vs: Leishmania amastigotes contain a kinetoplast and are negative on GMS and PAS, whereas Histoplasma yeasts stain with both.
Cryptococcus yeasts are larger (5-10 um), more variable in size, and have a mucicarmine-positive capsule.
Pneumocystis cysts are cup-shaped without internal dots, lie in foamy extracellular exudate, and do not occur within histiocytes as budding yeasts.
Talaromyces yeasts are elongated with a central transverse septum rather than budding; culture is often required.
